label: D2 with state S2 shown, early in the episode (trials < ~35)
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the state input is S2 (never on S1, D1 or GO), and only in the first ~35 trials of the episode: rate ~0.16-0.17 per D2 step in trials 0-29, drops in 30-39, and is zero from trial 50 on. So it is an S2-observation detector gated by time-in-episode. Magnitude decays steadily with episode trial (trials < 10 make up ~70% of the top quartile); it is also somewhat larger when S2 was reached by a rare transition (a1 -> S2, top windows reach 1.0 vs ~0.7 for common a2 -> S2). Not modulated by reward, stay/switch or core pattern. Uses only observed inputs (state input) plus the episode clock; ep_trial < 30 gives higher precision (0.98) but misses low-magnitude tail activations around trials 30-35.

issues: Minor factual error in the explanation. The 16-17% rate for trials 0-29 is the share of ALL steps in those trials, not of D2 steps. Among D2 steps that show S2 in trials < 30 the unit fires almost every time (test precision 0.975 for (phase==D2)&(in_state==2)&(ep_trial<30)). So early in the episode it is close to a deterministic S2 detector, which is stronger than the explanation says.

Checked and confirmed: zero activity at D1 and GO; zero on D2 steps showing S1 (F1 0.0); zero from trial 50 on; trials 40-49 have only 81 active steps on dev. The 30-35 band is weak and noisy (precision 0.46 there; 0.08 for trials 35-39). Trials < 10 cover 70% of the top activation quartile (matches the claim). Rare S2 is only modestly over-represented at the top: 35% of the top quartile vs about 22-23% in the other quartiles. The 'rare is larger' claim holds but is modest.

Test misses: 997 missed steps, 0.3% of activation mass, all tiny activations (<0.2) on S2 D2 steps just past the cutoff. 7098 false positives are S2 D2 steps near the trial-30-35 boundary, many with near-zero activations. Both are boundary effects of a gradual decay, not a systematic class. The magnitude also decays visibly across a window as ep_trial grows, which matches the decay over the episode.
start_high and good appear in the profile, but only through ep_trial and S2 frequency: precision stays at 0.87 vs 0.91 when split by start_high. No future variables are used.
